status: Closed — source and frozen runner published 2026-09-03
finding: `ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH` can report the same actor on both sides when the real mismatch is `ownershipMode: "lane-id"` and the holding lane session differs from the requested lane session. `ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID` also silently falls back to a newly minted lane when the supplied lane has stale TTL, so a caller can keep passing the documented env var and still fail renewal until running a separate lane adopt.
expectedBehavior: Lane-mode ownership mismatch should use a lane-specific error code and lane-vs-lane diagnostic payload. When a supplied lane session is stale but otherwise adoptable, the recovery path should either rebind/adopt it explicitly or fail with an actionable stale-lane error instead of silently minting a different session.
evidenceOrRepro: TASK-AAO-0206 close recovery on 2026-07-29: `tasks renew` printed `currentActor` and `actorId` as the same actor while data showed different `holdingLaneSessionId` and `requestedLaneSessionId`. A later retry with `ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID` still failed until `lane adopt` re-bound stale lease `lease-c461a4c70a22`.
followUp: Closed 2026-09-03: source commit `094e16a30a3732898359709c5230a30d5d8d597f` makes dual-lane lifecycle ownership mismatches emit `ATM_LANE_SESSION_OWNERSHIP_MISMATCH` with holding/requested lane ids and the existing lane-adopt recovery; actor-only fallback retains its prior caller-specific error code. Focused claim-owner, conflict-matrix, and dual-session adoption regressions plus typecheck passed. `lane adopt` already emits the exact `ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID` export hint, including stale-TTL adoption. Runner publication commit `3e49f5392ede8239ac618b1f53dda17403a3b9f5` was released through `runner-sync-395d5d88` with receipt digest `sha256:99a2a4d9f16ac1be9928d1186b059e09f661c8104fad64c706c946c4010a17c2`.
